tip: Before creating a Patient, call searchResources with unique attributes (e.g., family name, given name, birthDate, or identifier) to confirm the patient does not already exist and prevent duplicate records.
If the search bundle has total == 0 (no entries), branch to the “new patient” case and emit the required tag (e.g., <patient_id>new patient</patient_id>) instead of producing no output.
After calling searchResources, inspect bundle.total. If total=0, branch to the “new patient” logic; otherwise proceed to extract the existing patient’s ID.
When bundle.entry is non-empty, retrieve the ID via bundle.entry[0].resource.id and embed that value into <patient_id>…</patient_id>, avoiding hardcoded placeholders.
Call getSearchParams("Patient") before searching to confirm valid parameter codes (e.g., "name", "birthdate") and their types, then construct params_json accordingly.
After receiving a Bundle, inspect the "total" field: if total == 0, treat the patient as non-existent; otherwise pull the patient ID from each entry's resource.id.
Before creating a Condition, perform a search with parameters like subject=Patient/PAT001 and code=38341003 to detect any existing record and prevent duplicates.
Use a conditional create (e.g., add an If-None-Exist header with subject=Patient/PAT001&code=38341003) so the server only creates a new Condition if one does not already exist.
Call getSearchParams('Condition') to list and confirm valid search parameters (e.g., 'patient') before building your query, reducing trial-and-error.

Use the reference search parameter with full prefix (e.g., patient=Patient/{id}) to ensure correct matching. After the call, verify the Bundle contains both total and entry, and handle any non-200 responses by parsing the OperationOutcome for errors.

Include all required elements: status (e.g., draft|active|completed), intent (e.g., order|plan), subject.reference (Patient/{id}), code (CodeableConcept with valid coding), and use occurrenceDateTime to schedule the procedure date.
Use a valid CarePlan.status code from the official value set (proposed, draft, active, completed, suspended, cancelled, entered-in-error), not 'planned.'
Don’t use 'period-start' or 'period-end' – CarePlan supports the 'date' parameter for period-based queries. Run getSearchParams('CarePlan') to confirm valid params.
To find a surgery planned on a specific date, include subject, category and use the 'occurrence' date parameter (e.g., occurrence=2025-11-11) per getSearchParams('ServiceRequest').
CarePlan does not support period-start/period-end; use its valid date parameters (date or activity-date) by checking CarePlan searchParameters
To find scheduled services on a specific date, use occurrence=date (e.g., occurrence=2025-11-11) along with subject and category, as ServiceRequest supports occurrence but not period-start/period-end
Consult getSearchParams(ServiceRequest) first to see that date filtering uses the 'occurrence' parameter rather than unsupported keys like 'period-start' or 'period-end'.
Combine subject=PAT101, category=surgery (token), and occurrence=YYYY-MM-DD to find planned Surgery ServiceRequests on a specific date.

Include the mandatory RelatedPerson.patient reference pointing to Patient/PAT001 and set relationship using a CodeableConcept coding (system http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/relatedperson-relationshiptype, code 'father').
Populate subscriber.reference and policyHolder.reference with the RelatedPerson/{id} value (not just display) to ensure a resolvable link to the RelatedPerson resource.
After receiving the Bundle, verify that entry[0] exists, then extract entry[0].resource.id (e.g., “COV-PAT001”) and output it as <COVERAGE>id</COVERAGE>.
Verify that the returned Bundle.entry array has at least one element, then extract entry[0].resource.id and output it as <COVERAGE>id</COVERAGE> exactly as specified.

Use the full reference syntax for the beneficiary parameter (e.g. beneficiary=Patient/PAT101) since Coverage.beneficiary is a reference to Patient. This avoids ambiguity when servers require Type/ID format.
After the search, verify both bundle.total>0 and bundle.entry.length>0 before extracting the first entry’s resource.id. If either is zero, treat it as no coverage.

After receiving a successful createResource response (HTTP 201 with an id), capture and reuse the returned id instead of issuing another createResource. For idempotency, you can perform a conditional create (e.g., using an If-None-Exist header with patient and relationship) to prevent duplicate RelatedPerson records.
Cache the Patient/PAT001 resource after the initial getResourceById call to avoid redundant fetches of the same ID in the same session.
Add an Account.identifier (system|code) to the payload to enable idempotent operations and simpler lookup of the created account.
Only call getResourceById when you need the current resource state or versionId; skip it if you already have up-to-date data to reduce API calls.
Include an HTTP If-Match header with the current meta.versionId (e.g., If-Match: "W/\"1523\"") to enforce version-aware updates and prevent accidental overwrites.
When adding elements like guarantor, fetch the existing guarantor list and append the new entry instead of sending only the new list, to avoid unintentionally removing existing entries.
Use searchResources with the parameter subject=Patient/{id} to detect existing Accounts; interpret total==0 as “no existing Account” before creating one.
After confirming no existing Account, construct a new Account with status (e.g., “active”) and subject.reference set to "Patient/{id}", then call createResource.
If searchResources for Coverage with the patient returns zero entries, fallback to searching Account resources, as guarantor details often reside there.
Use the 'patient' (or 'subject') search parameter to find Account resources linked to the patient and inspect Account.guarantor.party.reference to retrieve the guarantor ID.
When searching by reference parameters like subscriber or beneficiary, include the full reference (e.g., subscriber=Patient/PAT001) rather than just the ID.
Add _include=Account:guarantor to the search query (e.g., ?subject=Patient/PAT001&_include=Account:guarantor) to retrieve the guarantor resource in the same bundle.
After extracting the guarantor reference (e.g., RelatedPerson/REL001), call getResourceById to confirm the guarantor’s existence and details.
Use the ‘patient’ search parameter (e.g., searchResources Account?patient=PAT101) to find any Account records linked to the Patient, which may contain guarantor information.
Parse each entry’s Slot.start as an ISO-8601 date/time, sort the bundle entries ascending by that field, then select the first entry to find the earliest slot.

After fetching the Bundle of Slot resources, extract each entry’s resource.start (instant), parse into datetimes, sort ascending, and then pick the first entry. Alternatively, include _sort=start in the search params to have the server return slots ordered by start time.
Use the ‘address’ search parameter to filter by city (e.g., address=Boston) alongside gender=female and communication=en in one query (Practitioner?gender=female&communication=en&address=Boston).
When more than one practitioner ID is found, iterate over each ID with schedule.actor to retrieve free slots, then compare slot.start timestamps across all results to identify the latest slot.
Include service-type=cardiology and status=free in your Slot search (e.g., Slot?service-type=cardiology&status=free) to fetch only available cardiology slots.
Use the schedule reference parameter (Slot?schedule=<ScheduleID>) or combine it with service-type to narrow slots to a specific Schedule ID returned earlier.
Derive the total slot count from the Bundle.total field of the Slot search response rather than manually counting entry elements.
After receiving the search Bundle, inspect the Bundle.total field. If total is 0, return exactly “No available cardiology slots found”. If total > 0, output <SLOT_COUNT>{total}</SLOT_COUNT>.

Use the 'actor' search parameter with Practitioner/{practitionerId} to filter slots for that provider; add status=free and sort or use start date comparators (lt, gt) to get the most recent available slot.

Use only the ‘start’ search parameter for time filtering. Supply both comparators by constructing params_json as a query string: e.g. "start=ge<startTime>&start=le<endTime>&status=free". Avoid unsupported parameters like ‘end’ and duplicate JSON keys.

When filtering by a date range on the same field (e.g. start), supply both prefixes in an array: {"start":["ge2025-10-28T05:34:30Z","le2025-10-28T17:00:00Z"],"status":"free"} instead of duplicating the key.
Validate search params with getSearchParams("Slot") to avoid unknown parameters like 'end'; use 'start' with comparators ge and le for date ranges.
After receiving a Bundle, if total equals 0 or entry array is empty, return exactly: 'No available slots for next Friday'.

Upon receiving an OperationOutcome with code ‘processing’ and diagnostics about an unknown parameter (e.g., ‘end’), call getSearchParams('Slot') to list valid search parameters (start, status, etc.) and remove unsupported ones.

To filter a date range on Slot.start, repeat the 'start' parameter with 'ge' and 'lt' prefixes (e.g., start=ge2025-10-31T00:00:00Z&start=lt2025-11-01T00:00:00Z) instead of using an unsupported 'end' parameter. Encode both values correctly (e.g., as an array) so neither is overwritten.
After getting the Bundle, post‐filter each entry’s start timestamp to ensure it falls on the exact target date (next Friday) before collecting slot IDs.
Use getSearchParams("Slot") to confirm that only “start” (not “end”) is supported for date filtering; then use “start=ge<date>” and “start=lt<date+1d>” to bound a one-day window.

When sending multiple comparators on the same parameter (e.g., ge and lt on “start”), ensure your query builder or params JSON supports multiple values rather than repeating the same key, which may override earlier entries.

Use the ‘start’ search parameter with comparators ‘ge’ and ‘lt’ to define a 1-day window (e.g., start=ge2025-11-27T00:00:00Z & start=lt2025-11-28T00:00:00Z). The Slot resource does not support an ‘end’ search parameter.
After receiving the Bundle, iterate over Bundle.entry[].resource.start and discard any slots whose start timestamps fall outside the target window, ensuring only matching slots are returned.

When specifying multiple constraints on the same code (e.g., start ge… and lt…), represent them as an array in the params JSON, e.g., "start":["ge2025-11-26T00:00:00Z","lt2025-11-26T12:00:00Z"] so both are sent without key collisions.
Add status=free to your search parameters to retrieve only available slots instead of all slots.
Because FHIR search doesn’t support filtering by day‐of‐week or morning time specifically, retrieve the date‐range bundle then client‐side filter each entry’s start date for Wednesday before 12:00.
After a searchResources call on Slot, iterate through bundle.entry[].resource.id to collect all slot IDs, then format them into the required tags (<SLOT_IDS> and <SLOT_COUNT>) before returning.
If a name search returns no entries, try splitting into 'family' and 'given' parameters or verify correct name casing and spelling.
Search using 'start=YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss' and 'schedule=Schedule/<schedule_id>' to pinpoint the exact slot time for that practitioner.
Use 'slot=Slot/<slot_id>' (and optionally 'practitioner=<practitioner_id>') to find the appointment booked in that slot.
Call getResourceById on the Patient reference from Appointment.participant.actor and extract only the id within <PATIENT_ID> tags.
Split the full name into family and given when searching (e.g. family=Smith and given=John) rather than a single 'name' parameter to improve matching.
After identifying a practitioner entry, call getResourceById with its id to load complete details before proceeding to dependent searches.
Use the 'practitioner' reference parameter set to Practitioner/{id} and the 'date' parameter with the exact dateTime (e.g. 2025-11-24T09:00:00) to find the specific appointment.
Extract the patient id from Appointment.participant where actor is a Patient, then call getResourceById on that id to retrieve the patient resource.
After obtaining the practitioner’s ID via getResourceById, call searchResources on Slot with actor=Practitioner/{practitioner_id} and start=<desired date/time> to find the correct slot.
Once you have the Slot ID, call searchResources on Appointment with slot=Slot/{slot_id} to locate the related appointment.
Extract the Patient reference from appointment.participant.actor, then use getResourceById on Patient/{patient_id} to retrieve the patient details and ID.
If Practitioner?name=FullName returns no results, split into given and family parameters (e.g. given=Jennifer&family=Anderson) to improve name matching.
Search Schedule by actor=Practitioner/{practitionerId} (e.g. Schedule?actor=Practitioner/123) to retrieve the practitioner’s schedule IDs before slot lookup.
Use Slot?schedule=Schedule/{scheduleId}&start=YYYY-MM-DDT09:00:00 to find the exact slot for the practitioner at the target date/time.
Query Appointment?slot=Slot/{slotId} to locate the booking associated with the found slot.
Take the patient reference from Appointment.patient (e.g. Patient/{id}) and call getResourceById to retrieve the Patient resource before extracting its ID.

Use the Appointment.slot element to include Slot references; do not place a Slot reference in Appointment.participant.actor. Check the Appointment StructureDefinition targetProfile for Appointment.participant.actor to ensure only Patient/Practitioner/etc. are used there.
Before updating a Slot, call getResourceById to retrieve its current state (including meta.versionId), then change only the status field to 'busy' while preserving other fields.

Include all mandatory elements: status (e.g., "booked"), start and end (ISO 8601 instants), and a participant array with actor references to both Patient and Practitioner. Without these, the server will reject creation or produce an empty result.
When marking a slot as filled, provide the Slot.id and set status to "busy". Ensure you reference the correct slot resource used in the Appointment.slot field to avoid updating the wrong slot.
After searching for a Patient, check if the Bundle.entry list is empty and emit a clear error if no matching patient is found before proceeding.
Fetch the current Appointment by its ID before updating to ensure you have the latest version and can supply the correct ETag if needed.
When cancelling an Appointment, set "status":"cancelled" and populate the "cancellationReason" element to comply with the Appointment status binding.
Fetch the current Slot by its ID before updating to ensure you have the latest version and correct ETag for concurrency control.
To free a Slot, update its "status" field to "free" in the Slot resource as per the Slot.status value set.
Use the ‘patient’ search parameter with the patient reference (e.g. ?patient=Patient/{id}&status=booked or date filters) to find the specific upcoming appointment.
Retrieve the Appointment by its ID to obtain the current meta.versionId before performing an update to avoid version conflicts.
Include the required status element (min=1) set to ‘cancelled’, preserve the resource id/version, and send the full Appointment resource when updating.
Fetch the Slot by its ID to get its current meta.versionId prior to modification.
Set the required status element (min=1) to ‘free’ when updating a Slot to release it.

When searching for an appointment, use both patient and practitioner reference parameters (e.g., patient=<Patient/id>&practitioner=<Practitioner/id>&status=booked) to reliably find the specific upcoming appointment.
Always fetch the full Appointment resource to retrieve its current versionId/ETag before performing an update to avoid concurrency conflicts.
Modify only the status element to ‘cancelled’; include the versionId (via If-Match) to ensure you’re updating the correct resource version.
After cancelling the appointment, fetch the referenced Slot by ID to get its current versionId for a safe update.
Update only the status element to ‘free’ to release the slot, and include the versionId (via If-Match) to prevent overwriting concurrent changes.
Use both patient=<Patient/id> and practitioner=<Practitioner/id> parameters to find the specific appointment for cancellation.
Before updating, fetch the Appointment by its id to obtain the latest version and slot reference.
When updating the Appointment, set status to 'cancelled' and preserve all existing fields (including slot) to avoid unintended data loss.
Extract the Slot id from Appointment.slot reference, then fetch that Slot resource before modifying it.
Update the Slot by id, set status to 'free', and include required fields (schedule, start, end) so the Slot remains valid.
Filter appointments by both 'patient=Patient/{patientId}' and 'date={YYYY-MM-DD}' to pinpoint the exact appointment on the given day
Include the Appointment.id and set the 'status' element to 'cancelled' in the payload to effect a cancellation
Use the Appointment.slot reference to fetch the Slot resource before making any changes
Preserve the Slot.id and change 'status' to 'free' in the payload to free up the slot
If a search with parameter 'name' returns zero matches, split the full name into 'given' and 'family' parameters (e.g., given=Michael, family=Smith) for more precise searching.
Use searchResources with 'patient=Patient/{id}' plus date filters (e.g., date=geYYYY-MM-DD&date=ltYYYY-MM-DD) to locate the specific appointment occurrence.

Before updating, fetch the Appointment with getResourceById to obtain the latest version, then set 'status' to 'cancelled' in the payload and include the current meta.versionId or use an If-Match header for safe concurrency.
Fetch the Slot via getResourceById, update its 'status' to 'free' (or 'available'), and include mandatory fields (start, end, schedule) in the update to preserve other data.

When creating an Appointment waitlist entry, include the required status (e.g., 'proposed' or 'pending'), set requestedPeriod with correct start/end instants (one day from now to six days later), and add participant entries referencing both the Patient and Practitioner (with required: 'required' or 'optional' and status: 'needs-action'). After creation, return the new resource.id wrapped in <APPOINTMENT>…</APPOINTMENT>.

Include Appointment.status='waitlist' (required), and at least one Appointment.participant entry per actor: set participant.actor to Patient/<id> and Practitioner/<id>, participant.required='required', participant.status='needs-action'.
Provide Appointment.requestedPeriod as an array with a Period: start = now+1 day, end = now+7 days, so server knows the waitlist window.
Use the supported ‘patient’ parameter (e.g., patient=PAT001) instead of ‘participant.identifier’; confirm with Appointment.searchParams first.
When filtering by practitioner, supply the actual FHIR reference (e.g., practitioner=Practitioner/PROVIDER001) to match the server’s ID, not a display name.
Slot does not support an ‘end’ search parameter; use only the ‘start’ parameter with ge/le comparators to constrain the time window.
Use the official 'patient' or 'actor' search parameter when filtering by patient on Appointment (e.g., Appointment?patient=PAT001), rather than unsupported codes like 'participant.actor:Patient'.
After finding an Appointment in the searchResults Bundle, call getResourceById on its ID to obtain the full resource before applying updates.
Include the complete Appointment resource body with updated 'status' (e.g., 'booked') and the new Slot reference in the 'slot' element when calling updateResource.
Once a slot is assigned to an Appointment, update the Slot resource's 'status' to 'busy' via updateResource to reflect the booking.
Use searchResources with params patient=PAT001 and status="waitlist" to reliably find a waitlisted Appointment. If zero entries return, prepare to handle the no-result case in your output.
Once you have the Appointment id, call updateResource with the full Appointment body setting status="cancelled" (and include any required fields) to cancel the appointment.
Use the ‘patient’ and ‘status’ search parameters together (e.g. {"patient":"PAT001","status":"proposed"}) to find waitlisted Appointments for the given patient in a single call.
When cancelling an Appointment, include its id and set the top-level status element to "cancelled"; preserve other mandatory elements (e.g. participant, meta) to avoid validation errors.
Use the standard search parameters ‘patient’ or ‘actor’ instead of ‘participant.actor’ when querying Appointment by patient reference.
Before updating the Appointment’s slot reference, call getResourceById on the target Slot to ensure its status is ‘free’.
When rescheduling, update both Slot resources: set the old Slot’s status to ‘free’ and the new Slot’s status to ‘busy’.
Use only supported search parameters for Slot (e.g. ‘start’, ‘schedule’, ‘status’). Remove invalid parameters like ‘end’ or use date comparators on ‘start’ for ranges.
Before updating an Appointment’s slot reference, fetch the target Slot and verify Slot.status is ‘free’; if not, choose a different slot or free it first.
Use the parameter 'patient' (not 'participant') to find appointments for a given patient, as 'participant' is not valid for Appointment searches.
Modify the existing Appointment by changing the slot reference and participant statuses. Preserve the resource’s id and meta.versionId and only alter the fields that need updating.
Update the old Slot to status='free' and the new Slot to status='busy' or 'booked', including its schedule reference, to reflect availability correctly.
Search for free slots by specifying both 'status=free' and the exact 'start' time to reliably locate available slots.
Use the 'patient' search parameter (not 'participant') when finding appointments for a patient—check Appointment.searchParams for valid codes.
The 'end' parameter is not supported on Slot; to filter by time window, use 'start' with range modifiers (e.g., start=ge2025-11-03T09:00:00Z&start=le2025-11-03T09:00:00Z).
To reschedule, call updateResource on the existing Appointment ID, modifying its start, end, and slot array rather than creating a new Appointment.
Release or claim a slot by updating its 'status' field (e.g., from 'busy' to 'free' or vice versa) via updateResource instead of creating/deleting the Slot.

Populate all required fields: set status='active', purpose='benefits', reference the patient and insurer, and include an insurance.backbone element with coverage reference. In item.productOrService use the correct coding for whole exome sequencing (system and code) so the insurer can evaluate the specific test.

After submitting the request, fetch the CoverageEligibilityResponse by its ID and inspect insurance[] elements—check insurance.inforce or applicable benefit entries to confirm whether the requested service is covered.

Before calling searchResources on Coverage, verify it isn’t prohibited by the task constraints. If searchResources is disallowed, use existing reference links on related resources or request the exact resource ID to fetch coverage details.
Detect HTTP 410 errors with issue.code 'processing' (e.g., resource deleted) and implement a fallback such as re-establishing or searching for the patient record before proceeding.

When creating a ServiceRequest for a lab test, include mandatory elements per the StructureDefinition: status (min=1, e.g. 'active'), intent (min=1, e.g. 'order'), subject (min=1, Patient reference), and code (use the correct LOINC code for the BRCA1 test).
If you receive an OperationOutcome with issue.code='processing' and diagnostics mentioning deletion, abort further GET attempts and report that the patient record is unavailable.
When creating a ServiceRequest, include a valid subject.reference in the form 'Patient/{id}' pointing to an existing, active Patient resource.
Combine the ‘given’ and ‘family’ search parameters in the initial query rather than using the generic ‘name’ parameter to locate the correct patient in one call.
Combine the ‘given’ and ‘family’ search parameters in the initial query rather than using the generic ‘name’ parameter to locate the correct practitioner in one call.
Use both 'given' and 'family' parameters in one searchResources call (e.g., ?given=Michael&family=Smith) to narrow results and avoid redundant queries.
Use combined 'given' and 'family' name parameters in a single search call to narrow down patient matches efficiently.
Include both 'category=genetics' and a specific 'code' filter (e.g., LOINC code for the genetic panel) in one search to directly locate relevant genetic reports.
Include a CodeableConcept.text element in condition.code to supply the human-readable term (e.g. text='breast cancer') alongside the coding to satisfy semantic expectations.
Before calling updateResource, use searchResources (e.g. subject + category) to retrieve the current ServiceRequest bundle entry, then update to ensure proper ordering and correct versioning.
Include a human-readable text in condition.code (CodeableConcept.text) matching ‘breast cancer’ alongside the SNOMED coding so downstream checks see the expected display.
Immediately fetch the specific ServiceRequest via getResourceById (using known ID) before updateResource to get the latest versionId and avoid multiple broad searches.

After performing createResource, parse the response to retrieve the ‘id’ value and wrap it exactly in the required <RESOURCE>…</RESOURCE> tags (or whatever custom delimiters the prompt mandates) before returning.
Before creating a FamilyMemberHistory, perform a searchResources by patient reference plus relationship and condition code to detect any existing history and prevent duplicate records.
